artist.artist_description: Led Zeppelin, formed in 1968, is renowned for pioneering hard rock and heavy metal genres. Their innovative sound, blending blues, folk, and rock, is showcased in classics like 'Stairway to Heaven' and 'Whole Lotta Love'. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1995.

Queen, formed in 1970, is celebrated for their eclectic style spanning rock, pop, and opera. Hits like 'Bohemian Rhapsody' and 'We Will Rock You' have become anthems, showcasing their theatrical performances and Freddie Mercury's powerful vocals. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2001.

The Eagles, formed in 1971, are known for their harmonious soft rock sound, epitomized by hits like 'Hotel California' and 'Take It Easy'. They have won six Grammy Awards and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1998. Their music continues to influence contemporary artists.

Bruce Springsteen, known as 'The Boss', has been a pivotal figure in rock music since the 1970s. His storytelling through songs like 'Born to Run' and 'Dancing in the Dark' captures the American experience. He has won 20 Grammy Awards and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1999.

Pink Floyd, formed in 1965, is famous for their progressive rock and psychedelic sound. Albums like 'The Dark Side of the Moon' and 'Wish You Were Here' are iconic, known for their thematic depth and innovative recording techniques. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1996.

The Clash, formed in 1976, were at the forefront of the punk rock movement. Their politically charged lyrics and diverse musical influences are evident in songs like 'London Calling' and 'Should I Stay or Should I Go'. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2003.

AC/DC, formed in 1973, is known for their high-energy hard rock and blues-based sound. Hits like 'Back in Black' and 'Highway to Hell' have made them one of the best-selling bands of all time. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2003.

Lynyrd Skynyrd, formed in 1964, is famous for their Southern rock sound, best known for 'Sweet Home Alabama' and 'Free Bird'. Despite numerous tragedies, including a plane crash in 1977, their legacy endures. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2006.

The Sex Pistols, formed in 1975, were central to the punk rock movement. Their rebellious attitude and raw sound are captured in 'Anarchy in the U.K.' and 'God Save the Queen'. Despite their short-lived career, their influence on punk and alternative music is profound.

Aerosmith, formed in 1970, is known for their blues-based hard rock sound. Hits like 'Dream On' and 'Walk This Way' have made them one of the best-selling American rock bands. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2001.

Deep Purple, formed in 1968, is renowned for pioneering heavy metal and hard rock. Their iconic track 'Smoke on the Water' is one of the most recognizable riffs in rock history. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2016.

Talking Heads, formed in 1975, are known for their innovative blend of new wave, punk, and art rock. Songs like 'Burning Down the House' and 'Once in a Lifetime' showcase their unique style and David Byrne's distinctive vocals. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2002.

The Police, formed in 1977, combined rock, reggae, and jazz influences. Hits like 'Every Breath You Take' and 'Roxanne' highlight their versatility and Sting's distinctive voice. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2003.

The Ramones, formed in 1974, are considered pioneers of punk rock. Their fast-paced, stripped-down sound is evident in songs like 'Blitzkrieg Bop' and 'I Wanna Be Sedated'. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2002.

Black Sabbath, formed in 1968, is credited with creating heavy metal. Their dark, heavy sound is showcased in classics like 'Paranoid' and 'Iron Man'. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2006.

Blondie, formed in 1974, is known for their blend of punk, new wave, and pop. Hits like 'Heart of Glass' and 'Call Me' highlight their versatility and Debbie Harry's iconic voice. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2006.

Boston, formed in 1975, is famous for their distinctive rock sound, characterized by Tom Scholz's innovative use of guitar effects. Their debut album, featuring 'More Than a Feeling' and 'Peace of Mind', is one of the best-selling debut albums in U.S. history.

Heart, formed in 1973, is known for their powerful rock sound and the vocal prowess of Ann and Nancy Wilson. Hits like 'Barracuda' and 'Crazy on You' showcase their talent. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2013.

Kansas, formed in 1970, is known for their progressive rock sound, blending rock with classical and jazz influences. Their epic 'Carry On Wayward Son' and 'Dust in the Wind' are iconic. They have a dedicated fanbase and continue to tour.

ZZ Top, formed in 1969, is known for their blues-based rock sound and signature beards. Hits like 'Sharp Dressed Man' and 'Legs' showcase their unique style. They were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2004.

Foghat, formed in 1971, is known for their blues-rock sound, with hits like 'Slow Ride' and 'Fool for the City'. Their energetic live performances and distinctive guitar riffs have earned them a loyal following. They continue to tour and record new music.

track.detail: Did you know that 'Stairway to Heaven' was crafted in a remote cottage in Wales? Robert Plant and Jimmy Page spent time there, and the song's lyrics were inspired by the natural beauty surrounding them. The track was recorded at Headley Grange, where the band used unconventional methods like recording in a hallway for that iconic guitar sound. It's fascinating to think that this song, which never was released as a single, still became one of the most requested songs on radio. Keep your radio tuned right here for more stories behind the music, and remember, we're all on this stairway together!

Did you know the song was almost not released because it was deemed too long for radio? But once it hit the airwaves, it soared to the top of the charts and became a cultural phenomenon.
